41:1: Surah Fussilat It is Meccan. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. God the Almighty says: “Ha Meem. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” This means the Qur’an was revealed from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, as in His saying: Say, ‘The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth.’ And His saying: “And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. * The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down * Upon your heart that you may be among the warners.” And His saying, the Blessed and Exalted: A Book whose verses are detailed, meaning its meanings are made clear and its rulings are perfected. An Arabic Qur’an, meaning that while it is an Arabic Qur’an, its meanings are clear and distinct, its words are clear and unmistakable, as in His saying, the Almighty: A Book whose verses have been perfected and then detailed from One Who is Wise and Acquainted, meaning it is miraculous in terms of its wording and meaning. “Falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it. A revelation from One Who is Wise and Praiseworthy.” And His saying, the Almighty: For a people who know, meaning only the well-established scholars know this clarification and clarity. As a bringer of good tidings and a warner, meaning sometimes He gives good tidings to the believers and sometimes He warns the disbelievers. But most of them turn away, so they do not hear, meaning most of the Quraysh, so they do not understand anything of it, with Its statement and clarity: “And they said, ‘Our hearts are within coverings’ meaning, covered in coverings, ‘from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness’ meaning, deafness to what you have brought to us, ‘and between us and you is a veil’ so nothing of what you say reaches us, ‘So work, indeed we are working’ meaning, you work according to your way and we will follow our way, we will not follow you. The learned Imam ‘Abd ibn Hamid said in his Musnad: Ibn Abi Shaybah told me, Ali ibn Musahhir told us, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, on the authority of Al-Ziyal ibn Harmalah Al-Asadi, on the authority of Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Quraysh gathered one day and said, ‘Look for the most knowledgeable of you in magic, divination and poetry. Let this man who has divided our community, scattered our affairs and criticized our religion come and speak to him, and let us see what he will say to him.’ They said, ‘We do not know anyone other than ‘Utbah ibn Rabi’ah.’ They said, ‘You, O Abu Al-Walid.’ So ‘Utbah came to him and said, ‘O Muhammad, are you better or ‘Abdullah?’” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent. He said, Are you better than Abdul Muttalib? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent. He said, “If you claim that these people are better than you, then they have worshipped the gods that you have criticized. But if you claim that you are better than them, then speak so that we may hear your words. By God, we have never seen a young lamb more ominous for your people than you. You have divided our community, scattered our affairs, criticized our religion, and disgraced us among the Arabs. It has even spread among them that there is a magician among the Quraysh and a soothsayer among the Quraysh. By God, we are only waiting for the cry of a pregnant woman, that some of us will rise up against each other with swords until we are annihilated. O man, if you are only in need, we will gather for you until you are the richest man of the Quraysh. But if you are in need, then choose any women of the Quraysh you wish, and we will marry you to ten.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Are you done? He said, Yes. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. “Ha Meem. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Until he reached, But if they turn away, then say, ‘I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of the heavens and the earth.’ The thunderbolt of Aad and Thamud. Utbah said, Enough, enough! You have nothing else to say. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, No. He returned to the Quraysh and they said, What is behind you? He said, I have not left anything that I think you will speak to him about, but I spoke to him. They said, Did he answer you? He said, No, by the One Who set it up, I did not understand anything of what he said except that he warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of Aad and Thamud. They said, Woe to you! The man speaks to you in Arabic and you do not know what he said? He said, No, by God, I did not understand anything of what he said except that he mentioned the thunderbolt. Abu Jahl said, “O people of the Quraysh, by God, we see that `Utbah has turned to Muhammad and liked his food. This is only because of a need that has befallen him, so let us go to him.” So they went to him and Abu Jahl said, “O `Utbah, what has kept you away from us is that you have turned to Muhammad and liked his food. This context is more similar to that of al-Bazzar and Abu Ya’la, and God knows best. Imam Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar included this story in his book, The Biography, in contrast to this pattern. He said, Yazid ibn Ziyad told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, who said: I was told that Utbah ibn Rabi’ah, who was a master, said one day while he was sitting in the gathering of the Quraysh and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting alone in the mosque: O people of Quraysh, should I not go to Muhammad and speak to him and present to him matters, perhaps he will accept some of them, so we can give him whichever he wants and he will desist from us? When Hamza, may God be pleased with him, converted to Islam and they saw the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, increasing in number, they said: Yes, O Abu al-Walid, go to him and speak to him. So, Utbah went to him and sat next to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O my nephew, you are one of us, as you know, of authority in the tribe and position in lineage. And you have come to your people with a great matter by which you have divided their unity, made fools of their dreams, criticized their gods and their religion, and disbelieved in those of their forefathers who have passed away. So listen to me, as I present to you matters for you to consider, perhaps you will accept some of them. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Say, O Abu al-Walid, I am listening. He said: “O son of my brother, if what you have brought is only wealth, we will collect for you from our wealth until you are the wealthiest of us. If you want honor, we will make you our leader so that we will not decide anything without you. If what you want is kingship, we will make you our king. If what has come to you is a vision that you see and cannot repel, we will seek doctors for you and spend our wealth on it until we cure you of it, because sometimes the follower will overcome a man until he is cured of it, or something like that. When Utbah had finished and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was listening to him, he said: “Have you finished, O Abu al-Walid?” He said: Yes. He said: Then listen to me. He said: I will. He said: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. “Ha Meem. * A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. * A Book whose verses are explained in detail - an Arabic Qur’an for a people who know * A bringer of good tidings and a warner.” But most of them turn away, so they do not listen. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) continued with it while he was reciting it to him. When Utbah heard it, he listened attentively and put his hands behind his back, leaning on them, listening to him until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) reached the prostration part of it. He prostrated and then said, O Abu al-Walid, you have heard what you heard, so it is up to you to decide. Utbah then went to his companions and some of them said to each other, We swear by God that Abu al-Walid has come to you with a face different from the one with which he left. When he sat down with them, they said, What is wrong with you, Abu al-Walid? He said, “Behind me, I heard a statement, and by God, I have never heard the like of it before. By God, it is neither magic, nor poetry, nor divination. O people of Quraysh, obey me and leave the man to me. Leave the man to what he is doing and isolate him, for by God, what I heard will be true. If the Arabs defeat him, you will have been sufficed with others, but if he prevails over the Arabs, then his kingdom will be your kingdom and his glory will be your glory, and you will be the happiest of people because of him.” They said, By God, O Abu al-Walid, he has bewitched you with his tongue. He said, This is my opinion of him, so do as you see fit. This context is more similar to the one before it, and God knows best.

And woe to the polytheists, meaning destruction and ruin for them. Those who do not give zakat. Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, meaning those who do not testify that there is no god but God. Ikrimah said the same. This is like the statement of God Almighty: “He has succeeded who purifies it. And he has failed who instills it with corruption.” And like His statement, may His Majesty be glorified: “He has succeeded who purifies himself. And remembers the name of his Lord and prays.” And the statement of God Almighty: Then say, ‘Would you like to be purified?’ What is meant by zakat here is purification. The soul from bad morals, and the most important of that is the purification of the soul from polytheism. The zakat of wealth is called zakat because it purifies it from what is forbidden and is a reason for its increase, blessing, and abundant benefit, and success in using it in acts of obedience. Al-Suddi said, Woe to the polytheists * Who do not give zakat, meaning they do not pay zakat. Muawiyah ibn Qurra said, They are not among the people of zakat. Qatada said, They prevent the zakat of their wealth. This is what is apparent according to many commentators, and Ibn Jarir chose it. There is a view in it because the obligation of zakat was only in the second year of the migration to Medina, according to what was mentioned by more than one person. This verse is Meccan, unless it is said that it is not far-fetched that the origin of charity and zakat was commanded at the beginning of the mission, as God Almighty said, And give its due on the day of its harvest. As for zakat, which has fixed amounts and quantities, its command was only mentioned in Medina, and this is a combination of the two opinions, just as the origin of prayer was obligatory before sunrise and before sunset at the beginning of the mission. When the Night of Isra' Journey to Heaven occurred a year and a half before the Hijra, God the Almighty imposed the five daily prayers on His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and explained their conditions, pillars, and related matters little by little, and God knows best. Then God the Almighty said after that: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have a reward uninterrupted. Mujahid and others said: "Not cut off or truncated, like His statement: "abiding therein forever," and His statement: "A gift uninterrupted." Al-Suddi said: "Not cut off from them." Some of the Imams rejected this interpretation, because God the Almighty bestows His favor upon the people of Paradise. God the Almighty said: "Rather, God confers a favor upon you that He has guided you to faith." The people of Paradise said: "So God has bestowed favor upon us and protected us from the torment of the poisonous winds." The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "Unless God covers me with His mercy and bounty."

41:19: God the Almighty says: And on the Day when the enemies of God are gathered to the Fire, they will be driven in ranks. That is, remind these polytheists of the Day when they will be gathered to the Fire, they will be driven in ranks, that is, the guards will gather them, the first of them to the last of them, as God the Most High said: And We will drive the criminals to Hell, thirsty. That is, their deeds of what they did in the past and the future, not a word of it will be concealed. And they will say to their skins, 'Why did you testify against us?' That is, they will blame their limbs and their skins when they testified against them. At that point, their limbs will respond to them. They will say, 'God has caused us to speak, He who has caused everything to speak, and He created you the first time.' That is, He does not oppose or hinder, and to Him you will be returned. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Will you not ask me about what I laughed about? They said: O Messenger of God, about what I laughed? The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “I am amazed at the servant’s argument with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He will say, ‘O my Lord, did You not promise me that You would not wrong me?’ He will say, ‘Yes.’ He will say, ‘Then I will not accept any witness against Me except myself.’ God, the Blessed and Exalted, will say, ‘Are not I and the noble recording angels sufficient witnesses?’ He will repeat this statement many times. It was you I used to argue with.’” Then he and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Amir al-Asadi from al-Thawri from Ubayd al-Maktab from Fudayl ibn Amr from al-Sha’bi. He said: So when he does that, his mouth will be sealed. Al-Ash’ari, may God be pleased with him, said: I think that the first part of his body to speak will be his right thigh. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Zuhair told us, Hasan told us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi`ah, Darraj said, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, the unbeliever will be known by his deeds, so he will deny and dispute. He will say, ‘These are your neighbors testifying against you.’ He will say, ‘They lied.’ He will say, ‘Your family and tribe.’ He will say, ‘They lied.’ He will say, ‘Swear.’ They will swear. Then God Almighty will silence them and their tongues will testify against them, and He will cause them to enter the Fire.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith told us, he heard my father say, Ali ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Muslim ibn Subaih Abu al-Duha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said to Ibn al-Azraq: “The Day of Resurrection will come upon the people at a time when they will not speak, nor apologize, nor talk until permission is given to them. Then permission is given to them, and they will dispute. The denier will deny his association with God Almighty, and they will swear to him as they swear to you. He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned.” So the tongues will be still after denial. That is, your limbs and skins will say to them when they blame them for testifying against them: “You were not concealing from us what you were doing. One of them said: Do you think that God hears our words? The other said: If we raise our voices, He hears them, but if we do not raise them, He does not hear them. The other said: If He hears something from it, He hears all of it. Mu’ammar said: Al-Hasan recited: And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord that has ruined you, then he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty said: ‘I am with My servant according to his assumption of Me, and I am with him when he calls upon Me.’” Then al-Hasan paused to consider this and said: “Behold, people’s actions are only according to the extent of their assumptions about their Lord. And that is your assumption which you assumed about your Lord that has ruined you.” The verse. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Nadr bin Ismail Al-Qass, who is Abu Al-Mughira, narrated to us, Ibn Abi Laila narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Let none of you die except while having good thoughts about God, for some people have been ruined by their bad thoughts about God. Quraysh used to do that. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And speak noisily during it, they criticize it. Qatada said: “Deny it, reject it, and oppose it. “That you may prevail.” This is the state of these ignorant disbelievers and those who follow their path when hearing the Qur’an. God, the Exalted, has commanded His believing servants to do otherwise, as God, the Exalted, said: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy. Then the Almighty said, defending the Qur’an and taking revenge on those who opposed it from among the disbelievers: Then We will surely make those who disbelieve taste a severe punishment, meaning in response to what they relied on in the Qur’an and when they heard it. Qatada said the same: Al-Hasan used to say, O God, You are our Lord, so grant us steadfastness. Abu Al-Aaliyah said, Then they remained steadfast, they devoted religion and deeds to Him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Say, ‘I have believed in God,’ then be steadfast. I said: What should I fear? He pointed to his tongue. An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ya’la ibn Ata’, with this chain of transmission. Then Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun told us, Ibrahim ibn Sa’d told us, Ibn Shihab told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma’iz al-Ghamidi, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Abdullah al-Thaqafi, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, tell me something that I may hold fast to. He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Say, ‘My Lord is God,’ then be steadfast. I said: O Messenger of God, what is the thing that you fear most for me? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) took hold of the tip of his tongue and said: This. And this is how At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Az-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission. At-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan sahih. Muslim included it in his Sahih, and al-Nasa’i included it on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Abdullah al-Thaqafi, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, tell me something about Islam that I will not ask anyone about after you. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Say, ‘I have believed in God,’ then be steadfast. And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. And the Almighty’s saying: The angels will descend upon them. Mujahid, As-Suddi, Zayd ibn Aslam and his son said: meaning at death, saying: Do not fear. Mujahid, Ikrimah and Zayd ibn Aslam said: meaning, regarding what you will face in the Hereafter. And do not grieve over what you left behind in this world, such as children, family, wealth or debt, for We will replace it for you. And receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised. They give them good tidings of the departure of evil and the attainment of good. This is as came in the hadith of Al-Baraa’ may God be pleased with him, who said: “The angels say to the soul of the believer: Come out, O good soul, in the good body that you inhabited. Come out to a spirit and fragrance and a Lord who is not angry.” It was said that the angels will descend upon them on the day they emerge from their graves. This was narrated by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Ibn Abbas and As-Suddi. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Abd al-Salam ibn Mutahhar told us, Ja’far ibn Sulayman told us, he said: I heard Thabit reciting Surah Ha Mim as-Sajdah until he reached: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain on a right course - upon them the angels will descend. Then he stopped and said: “It has reached us that when God raises a believing slave from his grave, the two angels who were with him in this world meet him and say, ‘Do not fear and do not grieve. And receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised.’” He said: So God will guarantee his fear from Him and will comfort his eyes. There is no greater fear people have on the Day of Resurrection than that it will be a comfort to the believer’s eyes because of God’s guidance to him and because of his deeds in this world. Zayd ibn Aslam said: They will give him good tidings at his death, in his grave, and when he is raised. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. This statement encompasses all the statements and is very good and is the reality. And the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: We are your allies in this world and in the Hereafter, meaning the angels will say to the believers when they are dying, “We were your allies in this world, guiding you, granting you success, and protecting you, and granting you success and protection by the command of God. And likewise, We will be with you in the Hereafter, keeping you company when you are lonely in the graves and when the Trumpet is blown, and keeping you safe on the Day of Resurrection and bringing you across the straight path and leading you to the Gardens of Bliss. “And therein you will have whatever your souls desire,” meaning in Paradise, from everything you choose of what your souls desire and what pleases your eyes. And therein you will have whatever you ask for, meaning whatever you ask for, you will find it and it will be presented to you as you chose. An accommodation from a Forgiving, Most Merciful, meaning hospitality and giving from one who is Forgiving of your sins, Merciful to you, Kind, as He forgives, conceals, has mercy, and is kind. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned here the hadith of the marketplace of Paradise, in the words of God the Almighty: “And therein you will have whatever your souls desire, and therein you will have whatever you request. An accommodation from a Forgiving, Most Merciful.” He said: My father told us, Hisham ibn Ammar told us, Abdul Hamid ibn Habib ibn Abi Al-Ashreen Abu Saeed told us, Al-Awza’i told us, Hassan ibn Atiyyah told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab, that he met Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, and Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, said: I ask God to bring me and you together in the marketplace of Paradise. Saeed said: Is there a marketplace in it? He said: Yes, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed me that when the people of Paradise enter it and descend due to the excellence of their deeds, permission will be given to them in the space of a Friday from the days of this world, and they will visit God the Almighty, and His Throne will be brought out to them and He will appear to them in a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and pulpits of light will be placed for them, and pulpits of pearls, and pulpits of rubies, and pulpits of emeralds, and pulpits of gold, and pulpits of silver, and the lowest of them, and the lowest among them, will sit on mounds of musk and camphor, and they will not see the owners of thrones in a better seat than themselves. Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him said: I said, O Messenger of God, will we see our Lord? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “Yes. Do you doubt seeing the sun and the moon on the night of the full moon?” We said, No. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “Likewise, you will not doubt seeing your Lord, the Most High, and no one will remain in that assembly except that God will attend to him, to the point that He will say to a man among them, ‘O so-and-so, son of so-and-so, do you remember the day you did such-and-such? ’ He will remind him of his treachery in the world, ‘O Lord, did You not forgive me? ’ He will say, ‘Yes, and it is by the breadth of My forgiveness that you have attained this station. ’ While they are in that state, a cloud will cover them from above and rain down upon them a perfume the likes of whose fragrance they have never known before. ’ He said, ‘Then our Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, will say, ‘Rise to what I have prepared for you of honor and take whatever you desire. ’ He said, ‘So we will come to a marketplace surrounded by angels, in which there is that which no eyes have seen the like of, no ears have heard, and no heart has imagined. ’ He said, ‘And whatever we desire will be brought to us. Nothing will be bought or sold there. ’ In that marketplace, people will find The people of Paradise will be with one another. He said: A man of high status will come forward and meet one of lower status. There will be no lowly person among them, and he will be startled by what he sees of clothing. No sooner has he finished speaking than he will be seen wearing something better than it. This is because no one should be sad there. Then we will return to our homes and our wives will meet us and say: Welcome to our beloved. You have come and you have more beauty and fragrance than what you left us with. He will say: Today we have sat with our Lord, the Almighty, the Blessed and the Exalted, and it is our right to return with the same as we returned with. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in Sifat al-Jannah in his Jami’ on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ismail on the authority of Hisham ibn Ammar. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Hisham ibn Ammar with a similar chain of transmission. Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a strange hadith that we do not know except from this source. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Abi Uday narrated to us on the authority of Humayd on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Whoever loves to meet God, God loves to meet him. Whoever hates to meet God, God hates to meet him.” We said: O Messenger of God, we all hate death. He said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “It is not a hatred of death, but when the believer is present and the bearer of good tidings from God Almighty comes to him regarding what he is destined to do. Mujahid, Ikrimah and Zayd ibn Aslam said: meaning, regarding what you will face in the Hereafter. And do not grieve over what you left behind in this world, such as children, family, wealth or debt, for We will replace it for you. And receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised. They give them good tidings of the departure of evil and the attainment of good. 41:33: God Almighty says: And who is better in speech than one who invites to God meaning invites God’s servants to Him and does righteousness and says, ‘Indeed, I am of the Muslims’ meaning he is guided in his own right by what he says, so his benefit to himself and others is both permanent and transitive. He is not one of those who enjoin what is right but do not do it and forbid what is wrong but do it. Rather, he enjoins what is good and abandons what is evil and invites people to the Creator, the Blessed and Exalted. This is general for everyone who invites to what is right and is guided in his own right, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the most deserving of this, as Muhammad ibn Sirin, al-Suddi, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said. It was said that what is meant by it are the righteous muezzins, as is proven in Sahih Muslim: The muezzins will have the longest necks on the Day of Resurrection. And in al-Sunan, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “The imam is responsible and the muezzin is trustworthy. So God guided the imams and forgave the muezzins.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn al-Harawi told us, Ghassan, the judge of Herat, told us. Abu Zur’ah said: Ibrahim told us. Ibn Tahman, on the authority of Matar, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, may God be pleased with him, that he said: “The arrows of the mu`adhdhins with God Almighty on the Day of Resurrection are like the arrows of the mujahidin, and between the call to prayer and the iqamah, he is like one who is immersed in the path of God Almighty in his blood.” He said: Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, said: If I were a mu`adhdhin, I would not mind not performing Hajj or `Umrah or fighting in jihad. He said: Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: “If I were a mu`adhdhin, my affair would be complete, and I would not mind not getting up for the night prayer or fasting during the day. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘O God, forgive the mu`adhdhins’ three times.” He said: “So I said: O Messenger of God, you left us while we were fighting over the call to prayer with swords.” He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, O Umar, a time will come upon the people when they will abandon the call to prayer for their weak, and that is flesh that God Almighty has forbidden to the Fire, the flesh of the mu`adhdhins. He said: Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: “And they have this verse: ‘And who is better in speech than one who invites to God and does righteousness and says, ‘Indeed, I am of the Muslims.’” She said: So he is the mu`adhdhin when he says, ‘Come to prayer,’ for he has invited to… God said: Thus, Ibn Umar may God be pleased with them both and Ikrimah said that it was revealed about the muezzins. Al-Baghawi reported on the authority of Abu Umamah al-Baahili may God be pleased with him that he said regarding the words of God the Almighty and Exalted: and does righteousness, meaning two rak’ahs of prayer between the adhan and the iqama. Then al-Baghawi included the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Mughaffal may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Between every two calls to prayer is a prayer, then he said on the third call to prayer: For whoever wishes. The group included it in their books on the authority of Abdullah ibn Buraydah on his authority, and the hadith of al-Thawri on the authority of Zaid al-Ami on the authority of Abu Iyas Muawiyah ibn Qurra on the authority of Anas ibn Malik may God be pleased with him, who said: Al-Thawri said: I think that he attributed it to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him): A supplication between the adhan and the iqama is not rejected. Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i narrated it in al-Yawm wa al-Laylah, all on the authority of al-Thawri on his authority. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan hadith. Al-Nasa’i also narrated it on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Anas on his authority. The correct view is that the verse is general in meaning to the muezzins and others. As for the time of revelation of this verse, the call to prayer was not legislated at all because it was revealed in Mecca, and the call to prayer was only legislated in Medina after the migration when Abdullah bin Abd Rabbih Al-Ansari may God be pleased with him saw it in his dream, so he narrated it to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who ordered him to recite it to Bilal may God be pleased with him, for he had the most melodious voice, as is stated in its place. So the correct view is that it is general, as Abd Al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he recited this verse: And who is better in speech than one who invites to God and does righteousness and says, ‘Indeed, I am of the Muslims,’ and he said: “This is the beloved of God, this is the friend of God, this is the chosen one of God, this is the best of God, this is the most beloved of the people on earth to God. God answered his call and called people to what God answered in his call and did righteousness in answering him and said, ‘Indeed, I am of the Muslims.’ This is the caliph of God.” And the Almighty’s saying: Not equal are the good deed and the bad, meaning there is a great difference between these two. Repel [evil] with that which is better, meaning whoever does evil to you, repel him from you by being kind to him, as Umar may God be pleased with him said: I do not punish anyone who has wronged you. Disobeying God in you is like obeying God in it. And the Almighty said: Then he between whom and you there was enmity will become as though he was a devoted friend. This means that if you do good to someone who has wronged you, that good deed will lead him to befriend you, love you, and be compassionate towards you until he becomes as though he were your devoted friend, that is, close to you in compassion and kindness towards you. Then the Almighty said: And none will receive it except those who are patient. That is, none will accept this commandment and act upon it except one who is patient in that, as it is difficult for the souls. And none will receive it except one who has a great portion. That is, one who has a plentiful share of happiness in this world and the hereafter. Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas in his interpretation of this verse: God commanded the believers to be patient when angry, to be forbearing when ignorant, and to forgive when wronged. So if they do that, God will protect them from Satan, and their enemy will submit to them as though he were a devoted friend. God the Almighty says: But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God. That is, the human devil may be deceived by being kind to him. As for the jinn devil, when he whispers, there is no trick except seeking refuge in the Creator who gave him power over you. If you seek refuge in God and turn to Him, He will restrain him from you and repel his plot. When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) stood up to pray, he would say: I seek refuge in God, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan, from his insinuations, his puffing, and his whispering. We have already mentioned that this position has no parallel in the Qur’an except in Surat Al-A’raf, when God the Almighty says: “Adopt forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant. But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.” And in Surat Al-Mu’minun, when He says: “Repel evil with that which is best. We know best what they describe. And say, ‘My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the insinuations of the devils. And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present.’”

41:44: When God the Almighty mentioned the Quran, its eloquence, rhetoric, and perfection of its wording and meaning, yet despite this the polytheists did not believe in it, He pointed out that their disbelief in it was a disbelief of stubbornness and obstinacy, as He the Almighty said: And if We had sent it down to some non-Arab * and he had recited it to them, they would not have believed in it. Likewise, if the Quran had been revealed as a whole in the language of non-Arabs, they would have said, out of stubbornness and obstinacy, Why are its verses not explained in detail? [Are they] a non-Arab and an Arab? That is, they would have said, Why was it not revealed in detail in the language of the Arabs? They would have denied that and said, A non-Arab and an Arab. That is, how can the words of a foreigner be revealed to an Arab who does not understand them? This meaning has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed ibn Jubayr, As-Suddi, and others. It was also said that what is meant by their saying, Why are its verses not explained in detail? Are they a non-Arab and an Arab? is, Were some of them revealed in a non-Arab language and some in Arabic? This is the saying of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and he used to read it like that without questioning in his saying foreign, and it is a narration from Saeed bin Jubair, and it is more eloquent in obstinacy and stubbornness. Then the Almighty said: Say, ‘It is, for those who believe, a guidance and a healing.’ That is, say, O Muhammad, this Qur’an is for those who believe in it, a guidance for their hearts and a healing for the doubts and suspicions in their hearts. And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, that is, they do not understand what is in it. And it is blindness for them, that is, they are not guided to what is in it of clarification, as the Almighty said: And We send down of the Qur’an that which is a healing and a mercy to the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss. “Those are being called from a place far away,” Mujahid said, meaning far from their hearts. Ibn Jarir said, its meaning is as if the one addressing them is calling them from a place far away, and they do not understand what he is saying. I said, “This is like the saying of the Almighty: ‘And the example of those who disbelieve is like that of one who shouts to that which hears nothing except calls and cries. Deaf, dumb, and blind, so they do not use reason.’” Ad-Dahhak said, They will be called on the Day of Resurrection. With the most hideous of their names. Al-Suddi said: Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him was sitting with a Muslim man who was giving a judgment when he said, O Labbayka! Umar may God be pleased with him said to him, Why did you respond? Did you see anyone or did anyone call you? He said, A caller from across the sea called me. Umar may God be pleased with him said, Those are the ones calling from a distant place. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And the words of God, the Most High: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, but it was disputed over meaning, he was lied to and harmed. So be patient, as were patient the messengers of strong will. “And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term” by delaying the reckoning until the Day of Judgment. Then it would have been judged between them meaning, the punishment would have been hastened for them. Rather, they have an appointment from which they will find no refuge. And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt about it. Meaning, their denial of him was not based on their insight into what they said. Rather, they were doubting what they said, not confirming anything they were in. This is how Ibn Jarir interpreted it, and it is possible, and God knows best.

41:52: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who deny the Qur’an, Have you considered if this Qur’an was from God and then you disbelieved in it? That is, how do you see your situation before the One who sent it down to His Messenger? And for this reason the Almighty said: Who is more astray than he who is in extreme dissension? That is, in disbelief, stubbornness, opposition to the truth, and a path far from guidance. Then the Almighty said: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves. That is, We will show them Our proofs and arguments that the Qur’an is the truth revealed from God to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with external proofs. In the horizons are the conquests and the emergence of Islam over the regions and all other religions. Mujahid, al-Hasan, and al-Suddi said: And proofs within themselves. They said: The Battle of Badr, the conquest of Mecca, and similar incidents that befell them, in which God granted victory to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, and in which falsehood and its party were defeated. It is possible that what is meant by this is what man is composed of, in, and upon, of materials, mixtures, and wondrous forms, as is explained in detail in the science of anatomy, which indicates the wisdom of the Creator, may He be blessed and exalted. Likewise, what he is created with of varying morals, of good and bad, and other things, and what he is disposed of under the decrees that cannot be estimated by His power, strength, and tricks. He warned him not to exceed it and not to go beyond it, as Ibn Abi Al-Dunya recited in his book Al-Tafakkur wa Al-I’tibar on the authority of his Sheikh Abu Jaafar Al-Qurashi, where he said in the best way: If you look, wanting someone to take heed, then look at yourself, for in you there is someone to take heed. You are the one who goes to bed and wakes up in this world, and all of its affairs are lessons. You were a small bank, then you became independent as an adult. You are the one whose creation mourns him, and poetry and humanity mourn him for him. You are the one who gives and takes away, and that does not save him from being robbed of caution. You are the one who has no more right to what is due to Him than anything else. God the Almighty said: {until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not sufficient for your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?} meaning, God is sufficient as a Witness over the actions and words of His servants, and He bears witness that Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is truthful in what he has informed us about Him, as He said: {But God bears witness to what He has revealed to you, [O Muhammad] - He sent it down with His knowledge} [verse].
